prompt: explain what happens in React when state changes and the screen updates

keyLinks.cause: The state setter (e.g. setState) is called
keyLinks.effect: React schedules a re-render of that component
keyLinks.mechanism: Calling the setter tells React state changed; the current render's variables are not changed in place

keyLinks.effect: The component function runs again with the new state and returns new JSX
keyLinks.mechanism: Rendering is calling the component to describe what the UI should look like now

keyLinks.effect: Its children re-render too by default
keyLinks.mechanism: Children are part of the parent's returned output unless memoized

keyLinks.cause: React has a new description of the UI
keyLinks.effect: It compares it with the previous one (reconciliation)
React updates only those parts of the real DOM (commit)
keyLinks.mechanism: Changing only what differs avoids rebuilding the page

keyLinks.effect: The browser paints the update and the screen changes
keyLinks.mechanism: The browser redraws changed parts of the page
Effects run after React has updated the DOM

knownErrors.claim: Changing state directly (e.g. array.push or obj.x = 1) triggers a re-render
knownErrors.why: Only calling the state setter with a new value schedules a re-render

knownErrors.claim: State updates immediately, so the next line of code sees the new value
knownErrors.why: The new value is available on the next render

knownErrors.claim: React re-renders by replacing the whole DOM / whole page
A child component only re-renders when its props change
knownErrors.why: By default children re-render whenever their parent re-renders

knownErrors.claim: useEffect runs during rendering or before the screen updates

acceptableSimplifications: Calling the render output a "drawing" or "plan" of the screen
Merging reconciliation and commit into one step
Omitting batching, concurrent rendering and memoization
